# Storyboard — Concept 2, the audit cycle (the PDSA wheel)

Question: **What does it take to make the safe thing the fast thing?**

A sticky header runs the full height of the page: her name, her two titles, a rail that jumps to any chapter, and a contact link that skips straight to the close. This is what carries a visitor who does not scroll — see "Someone with thirty seconds" below.

## The chapters

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open | Plan (closing) | The opening | The question; the night that started it, with nothing identifying | A complete wheel sits at rest, unlit, one quarter-turn from closing | Scroll only |
| Who | — (hub) | Who | Her name, both titles, 11 years, 6 of them in charge | The hub lights, the four wedge outlines appear | Hover a title for what it means |
| Plan | Plan | Where from / How | The years and places; the tools she reads a ward by | The Plan wedge fills with a timeline and four tool icons | Click a tool icon for a one-line description; click a year for the place |
| Do | Do | What | 40 hours of observation, 22 interviews, three workarounds, none of them laziness | The Do wedge fills; three panels appear | Click a panel to open the workaround it names |
| Study | Study | What came of it | The fixes; scanning compliance rising | The Study wedge fills; a number counts from 71 to 94 | Hover the number for how it was measured |
| Act | Act | What came of it | The handover sheet on six wards; 14 nurses precepted; two dashboards built | The Act wedge fills; six small ward marks, a tally, two named panels | Click a ward mark to see it is one of six |
| Close | Plan (new) | The close | The question, answered; how to reach her | The wheel completes its turn and settles, one quarter left open | Contact link; rail |

## The beats

### Open

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | The wheel, whole, facing the visitor dead-on, like a cycle poster pinned to a noticeboard | Nothing printed yet — the wedges are blank | A proof strip beneath the wheel: "71% to 94% in nine months" | **What does it take to make the safe thing the fast thing?** |
| 2 | 1 | The wheel begins its first slow turn | Still blank | Nothing | She started asking it the night a medicine nearly reached the wrong patient, because the nearest scanner was at the other end of the ward. |

### Who

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 1 | The wheel's hub, centred, the four wedge outlines now visible around it | Her name and both titles, printed on the hub | Nothing | **Aoife Brennan.** CNM1 on a 28-bed cardiac step-down ward, and one day a week, Nursing Informatics Link Nurse — eleven years a nurse, six of them in charge of a shift, at St Brendan's University Hospital. |

### Plan

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 1 | The Plan wedge fills first; a thin timeline runs along its arc | 2011 BSc General Nursing · 2015 Staff Nurse, Coronary Care Unit · 2019 CNM1, Cardiac Step-Down · 2024 MSc Health Informatics (in progress) | Nothing | Where she's been, in order. |
| 5 | 1 | Four small tool icons sit inside the same wedge | ISBAR handover · the early warning score chart · the care plan · the audit cycle itself | Nothing | What she reads a ward by, every shift. |

### Do

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 2 | The Do wedge fills; three panels open from it, side by side | Panel 1: a wristband that won't scan after a shower. Panel 2: a scanner kept on a trolley, away from the medication room. Panel 3: a printed sheet of barcodes, kept in a pocket | Nothing | Forty hours watching two cardiac wards, day and night, and short interviews with 22 nurses. Three workarounds accounted for most of the missed scans. None of them was laziness — each saved a nurse one to four minutes a round. |

### Study

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 2 | The Study wedge fills; a single number sits at its centre, climbing as the visitor scrolls | 71 → 94 | A thin trace line under the number, rising | Scanners moved to the medication room door. The wristband stock changed. The printed sheets stopped. Scanning rose from 71% to 94% in nine months. |

### Act

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1 | The Act wedge fills; six small marks appear in a row | The ISBAR handover sheet she led the redesign of, shown blank | Nothing | She led a group of five on the redesign. It's now the handover on six wards. |
| 9 | 1 | Beside the six marks, a tally and two named, unopened panels | "14 nurses precepted" · "Falls audit dashboard" · "Pressure ulcer audit dashboard" | Nothing | Fourteen newly qualified nurses precepted. Dashboards built for two more audits — not shown here; ask her if she can send one, cleared of patient data, before these go further than a name. |

### Close

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 1 | The wheel completes its turn and comes to rest, whole — except the Plan wedge, left a little open | Her name again; a line for contact | A soft light in the open wedge | That's what it takes: watch how the work really happens, then fix the thing that's in the way. She's looking to do this full time, from 2026. [Get in touch — email to be added] |

## Someone with thirty seconds

The sticky header gives the first three without any scroll: her name and both titles, and a contact link. The first screen (Open, beat 1) gives the fourth: the proof strip, "71% to 94% in nine months," sitting under the still wheel. The rail in the header jumps to any chapter; its contact link skips straight to the close.

## Without the scene

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | The wheel becomes four stacked cards, Plan/Do/Study/Act, in page order, each filling in as it's reached. Hover becomes tap: tapping a tool icon, a workaround panel, or a ward mark opens it in place. The header collapses to a thin bar with the name, a menu icon for the rail, and the contact link. |
| With reduced motion | No turning, no counting up. Each beat appears already in its settled state as it's scrolled to — the 94 is just there, not counted to. The wedges fill in one flat step, not a sweep. |
| With no WebGL | The wheel is drawn flat, in CSS or SVG: four coloured quarters in a ring, same labels, same numbers, same click targets. Nothing shown here depends on 3D to be understood. |
| With no JavaScript | A plain HTML page, chapters in order top to bottom, same captions, same figures, the blank handover sheet and the workaround panels as ordinary images and text. The rail is a set of anchor links. Nothing in the page's meaning is only in the scene — the text carries the full story on its own. |

## The look and the type

Three directions, from the wheel's own material. She picks once it's built and she can scroll it.

- **Ward noticeboard.** Ground: matte off-white, like poster card. Ink: charcoal. One accent: the red used for an early-warning score that's tripped — kept for the proof numbers and nothing else. Pieces: flat, printed-looking, like a QI poster pinned to cork.
- **Night shift.** Ground: near-black navy, the ward at 3 a.m. Ink: warm off-white. One accent: a cool monitor-trace teal, for the active wedge and the climbing number. Pieces: a faint glass sheen, softly lit from inside.
- **Day shift.** Ground: warm kraft tan, like a clipboard. Ink: ballpoint blue. One accent: a muted clinical green, saved for "94" and nothing before it. Pieces: a slightly worn paper texture.

Two typefaces. One for the running text: a plain, humanist sans, built to be read at length, not a display face. One for what's printed on the wheel itself — the labels, the numbers, the wedge names — a condensed, slightly institutional sans, the kind printed on a hospital form or a wristband, used nowhere else on the page.

## Everything else the site needs

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | Build — one continuous scroll, with the header rail as the only other way through | Me, as the shape the concept needs |
| A page for each project | Never — a second page would split the one wheel this concept turns on | Me |
| Every project listed | Build, inside Do/Act — the poster study, the handover redesign, the two dashboards (named, not shown) | Me |
| How to reach them, and a CV | Contact link: build. A downloadable CV: **ask her** — does she want one attached, and does she have a file for it? | Her to decide |
| What others say | Never, for now — nothing in the material is a quote from someone else. If her manager or a colleague gives her a line, it can be added later, with that person's yes first | Me, flagged for later |
| Languages | **Ask her** — English only, or Irish as well? | Her to decide |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | Build — needs a small share image and an icon. **Ask her** whether the wheel motif should be the icon, or something plainer | Her to decide the look; build either way |
| The page for an address that is not there | Build — simple, on the same material: the wheel stuck mid-turn | Me |
| A blog | Never — nothing in the material calls for one | Me |
| A chat | Never | Me |
| A legal notice | **Ask her** — only needed if the site uses analytics or cookies. If she wants to know who's visited, that brings a notice with it; if not, it isn't needed | Her to decide |

## What I'm asking for

A yes to this script, or what to change in it. Everything I decided without asking is listed above and in `docs/story/decided-for-you.md`, each with how to change it.

The sticky header gives the first three without any scroll: her name and both titles, and a contact link. The rail in the header jumps to any chapter; its contact link skips straight to the close.

## Without the scene

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | The wheel becomes four stacked cards, Plan/Do/Study/Act, in page order, each filling in as it's reached. Hover becomes tap: tapping a tool icon, a workaround panel, or a ward mark opens it in place. The header collapses to a thin bar with the name, a menu icon for the rail, and the contact link. |

- **Day shift.** Ground: warm kraft tan, like a clipboard. Ink: ballpoint blue. One accent: a muted clinical green, saved for "94" and nothing before it. Pieces: a slightly worn paper texture.

Here's the full script, saved to `docs/story/storyboard.md`. In full:

## The idea
Question the whole page answers: **What does it take to make the safe thing the fast thing?** — your own words, turned forward. The object is a **PDSA wheel** — Plan, Do, Study, Act — the cycle you already named as something you work from, and, not by coincidence, the exact shape your poster study already took. A sticky header (name, both titles, a jump-rail, a contact link) runs the whole page, so anyone who never scrolls still gets the essentials.

## Scrolling top to bottom

**Open.** A complete wheel sits at rest, unlit, one quarter-turn from closing — like a cycle poster pinned to a noticeboard. Under it: "71% to 94% in nine months." As you scroll, it begins its first slow turn, and the caption says why she started asking: *"the night a medicine nearly reached the wrong patient, because the nearest scanner was at the other end of the ward"* — no bed, no initial, no drug.

**Who.** The hub lights up with her name, both titles, and "eleven years a nurse, six of them in charge of a shift."

**Plan.** The first wedge fills: a timeline (2011 BSc → 2015 Coronary Care → 2019 CNM1 → 2024 MSc, in progress), then four small tool icons for what she reads a ward by — ISBAR, the early warning chart, the care plan, the audit cycle itself.

**Do.** The second wedge fills, opening three panels: a wristband that won't scan after a shower, a scanner kept too far from the medication room, a printed sheet kept in a pocket. Caption: 40 hours of observation, 22 interviews, "none of them was laziness."

**Study.** The third wedge fills around a single number climbing from 71 to 94, under a thin rising trace line. Caption: what actually changed — scanners moved, wristbands changed, sheets stopped.

**Act.** The fourth wedge fills: six marks for the six wards now using her handover redesign, a tally for 14 nurses precepted, and two dashboards named (not shown — no screenshot exists yet).

**Close.** The wheel completes its turn and settles whole, except the Plan wedge is left a little open — her next move. Caption states the answer plainly and that she's looking to do this full time from 2026, with a contact link.

## What moves, what's clickable
The wheel turns a quarter-turn per chapter, wedges filling with real figures as you go. You can hover a title for what it means, click a tool icon or a workaround panel to open it, hover the 71→94 number to see how it was measured, click a ward mark to confirm it's one of six. The rail jumps to any chapter; one link skips straight to Close.

## Without the 3D
- **Phone:** the wheel becomes four stacked cards (Plan/Do/Study/Act) filling in as you scroll to them; hover becomes tap; the header collapses to a thin bar with a menu icon.
- **Reduced motion:** no turning, no counting up — each beat just appears in its settled state.
- **No WebGL:** the wheel is drawn flat in CSS/SVG, same labels, same numbers, same click targets.
- **No JavaScript:** a plain HTML page, chapters stacked in order, same text and figures, nothing lost — the scene is decoration over a page that stands on its own.

## Look and type
Three directions, all from the wheel's own material — you pick once it's built:
- **Ward noticeboard** — matte off-white, charcoal ink, one early-warning red kept only for the proof numbers.
- **Night shift** — near-black navy, warm off-white ink, a monitor-trace teal for the active wedge.
- **Day shift** — kraft tan, ballpoint blue ink, a muted clinical green saved for "94."

Two typefaces: a plain humanist sans for running text, and a condensed, institutional-looking sans — like what's printed on a hospital form — used only for what's printed on the wheel itself.

## Everything else, and who decides
- **Build:** one continuous scroll with a rail; the three real projects folded into Do/Act; a 404 page (the wheel stuck mid-turn); a share-image and site icon.
- **Never:** a page per project, a blog, a chat — nothing in your material calls for them.
- **Later, if it comes:** a quote from a colleague or manager, once they've said yes to being quoted.
- **I need your answer on:** a downloadable CV (do you want one, do you have a file?), English only or Irish as well, what the site's icon should look like, and whether you want analytics — which would mean a short privacy notice.

Full detail, including every beat and every decision I made without asking (with how to undo each), is in `docs/story/storyboard.md`, `decided-for-you.md`, `concepts.md`, and `facts.md`. Building isn't part of this version — once you say yes to this script (or tell me what to change), that's the end of the plan.
